description: We are a fast-moving, multi-disciplinary team with a track record of competitive hackathon success, including a past NASA Space Apps Global Nomination. Our core strengths lie at the intersection of first-principles engineering and cinematic storytelling. We specialize in building highly performant, zero-dependency web applications (Vanilla JS, HTML5 Canvas) and crafting high-quality multimedia pitches that clearly sell a technical vision.
summary:
Red Outpost began with a simple question: What would it take to keep four astronauts alive on Mars?

We developed an interactive mission simulator where students aged 7–12 take command of a four-person crew during a 30-sol Mars mission. Their task is to keep the habitat running, manage limited resources, and respond to unexpected mission challenges.

The simulation brings together five interconnected systems: power management, life support, food production, radiation protection, and Earth–Mars communication. Every decision has consequences. Students must balance competing needs, respond to solar storms, and protect their crew when conditions change.

We grounded the experience in scientific data, research, and models from NASA and other space-science institutions. These inform our Mars environment, terrain, planetary calculations, radiation scenarios, and MOXIE-inspired oxygen production system.

We also wanted the experience to be accessible to more learners, so Red Outpost supports offline gameplay and both English and Bangla. Its Flight Director's Review helps students understand the outcomes of their decisions.

Our goal is to make learning about space more than memorizing facts. We want students to experience the challenges of exploration, think like mission commanders, and develop the skills to solve problems.

Red Outpost

Red Outpost is an offline-first, interactive Mars survival simulator that places students aged 7–12 in command of a four-person astronaut crew on a 30-sol mission. It transforms space education into experiential learning, where every decision has consequences and students must balance limited resources to keep their crew alive.

The simulation integrates five interconnected survival systems: power management, life support and MOXIE-inspired oxygen production, hydroponic food cultivation, radiation protection, and Earth–Mars communication delays. Students select landing sites, monitor environmental conditions, allocate energy, manage crew activities, and respond to solar storms and other mission challenges. A Flight Director's Review compares their decisions against an autonomous reference strategy, helping them understand the consequences of their choices.

Scientific Foundation: We incorporated verified scientific datasets, research and mathematical models from NASA and JPL, including DONKI WSA-ENLIL solar weather simulations, MOLA elevation data, InSight weather observations, NASA GISS Mars24 calculations, JPL planetary ephemerides, and NASA life-support research. These sources inform the simulation's environmental conditions, terrain hazards, energy generation, radiation scenarios and communication delays. Scientific approximations are documented transparently.

Technology Stack: The application is built using TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3 and Vite, with a lightweight custom DOM architecture. SVG and Canvas power the interactive habitat visualization, terrain radar, telemetry and charts. Native Web Audio API generates procedural sound effects, while LocalStorage, service workers and PWA technologies support offline functionality. Vitest, Playwright and ESLint support testing and code quality. No dedicated external hardware is required.

Creativity and Design Considerations: Our key innovation is connecting scientific models with meaningful survival trade-offs rather than presenting space science as conventional quizzes. We prioritized scientific credibility, deterministic and reproducible simulations, child-friendly interaction, accessibility, mobile compatibility, bilingual English and Bangla learning, privacy and low-bandwidth usability. All scientific datasets are compiled into the application during development, allowing the simulator to operate without runtime network requests.

Our intended impact is to develop scientific curiosity, systems thinking, resource management and critical decision-making among young learners, inspiring them to become active participants in humanity's future beyond Earth.
